threads.gloss: take account of, attend to; call to account; appoint, put in charge

opens.note: paqad opens the book: the two censuses (1, 26) and the Levite counts (3–4) are built on it; later it turns to ‘call to account’ (14:18, 29).

payoffs.note: Levi again stands outside the account (1:47); the same rare ‘were not accounted’ returns for the second generation at 26:62.
paqad turns from counting to appointing: Aharon and his sons are 'put in charge' of their priesthood.
Levi is accounted for from a month old, not twenty: a devoted tribe, not an army, and the count must come out exact.
Counting turns to oversight and inventory: Elazar's oversight (4:16), appointments (4:27), and vessels accounted for by name (4:32).

opens.note: tsavaʾ, the fighting force Israel is accounted into; 4:3 reuses it for Levite service at the tent and 31 for the Midian campaign.

payoffs.note: The fighting-force word turned to Levite duty: they 'come into the army' to do work at the Tent of Meeting.

threads.gloss: community, assembly gathered as one body

opens.note: ʿedah, Israel as one assembled body; it becomes the actor that complains, rebels and is judged (14:1–2, 16:3, 20:1–2).

payoffs.note: The community owes the sanctuary's upkeep; the Levites keep its charge on its behalf.

threads.gloss: charge, guard-duty, what one keeps watch over

opens.note: mishmeret, the Levites’ and priests’ ‘charge’ that structures chs. 3–4 and 18.

payoffs.note: mishmeret becomes the chapter's organizing noun: the Levites keep Aharon's charge and the whole community's.
The leaders camp at the east entrance 'keeping the charge of the holy place', the most exposed post in the camp.
Charge now names each house's load, assigned and supervised by the priests (4:27–33); Lev 8:35 tied keeping it to not dying.
